rows.selection_reason: 1) No prior evidence exists; the design space spans modality (RNA/image/multimodal), encoder choice, profile setting, aggregation, and fusion. The largest uncertainty is whether any single modality or encoder dominates, and we need a clean reference point. 2) config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest RNA baseline: a standard linear encoder, one profile, no aggregation or fusion. It isolates the contribution of RNA data with a well-understood representation. 3) Establishing this baseline first is the best use of experiment 1 because it is fast to train, unambiguous in interpretation, and provides the anchor against which all subsequent experiments (image-only, multimodal, alternative encoders, multiprofile) can be compared. With 9 experiments remaining, this reference will let me efficiently decide whether to invest in better RNA encoders, image modalities, or multimodal fusion.

The only completed experiment (config_001, rna_only/singleprofile/pca_n2000) yielded a low accuracy of ~48.5%, giving us a weak baseline with no information about whether image features carry useful signal. The most critical uncertainty at this stage is whether the image modality is informative at all, since it determines whether multimodal fusion is worth pursuing. Config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) is the cleanest single-variable comparison to config_001: it changes only the modality while keeping profile setting (single) and encoder complexity comparable. If image_only substantially outperforms the RNA baseline, it signals that image features are the stronger signal and multimodal configs become high-priority. If it performs similarly or worse, we can focus remaining budget on RNA encoder improvements (scvi, scgpt) and multiprofile aggregation. With 8 experiments left, resolving this fundamental modality question early prevents wasting budget on multimodal configurations that may not help.

Evidence: config_001 (RNA, single-profile, PCA n2000) achieved 0.485 acc, while config_010 (image, ResNet50) was very weak at 0.208 acc, establishing RNA as the dominant modality. The key uncertainty is whether a learned RNA encoder (scvi) can substantially outperform the PCA baseline, since the encoder choice is a fundamental design axis that propagates to all multiprofile and multimodal configurations. This experiment (config_004: RNA-only, single-profile, scvi_n200) is a clean single-variable comparison against config_001, isolating the encoder effect. If scvi improves meaningfully over PCA, it justifies prioritizing scvi-based multiprofile and multimodal configs in the remaining 7 experiments; if it does not, PCA remains the preferred encoder and budget can focus on profile/aggregation/fusion. This is the highest-information-per-experiment choice given the sparse evidence.

Evidence: scvi_n200 (0.5203) outperforms pca_n2000 (0.4849) by ~3.5% in the rna_only/singleprofile setting, and image-only resnet50 is very weak (0.2079), confirming RNA is the dominant signal. Uncertainty: We have not yet tested scgpt, the third available RNA encoder, so we don't know which encoder is optimal. This experiment (config_007: rna_only, singleprofile, scgpt) completes a clean three-way RNA encoder comparison under identical conditions, isolating the encoder effect. This is the best use of experiment 4 because the RNA encoder choice will propagate into all subsequent multimodal and multiprofile configurations; knowing the best encoder before committing to more complex fusion/aggregation experiments (which consume 2+ budget slots) maximizes the value of the remaining 6 experiments. If scgpt substantially outperforms scvi_n200, we pivot to scgpt-based configs; if not, we confidently exploit scvi_n200 for multiprofile and multimodal tests.

Evidence: scvi_n200 is the best RNA encoder (acc=0.520, F1=0.498), clearly outperforming pca_n2000 (0.485) and scgpt (0.411). Image-only with resnet50 is very weak (0.208), suggesting RNA dominates. All four completed experiments used singleprofile; multiprofile has not yet been tested. Question: Does multiprofile with avgpool aggregation improve upon the best singleprofile result (0.520) for scvi_n200? This is a clean single-variable change (singleprofile → multiprofile + avgpool) that isolates the effect of multi-profile aggregation. Choosing avgpool over transformer first is the more conservative test: if simple averaging of profiles helps, it confirms multiprofile is beneficial and justifies testing transformer next; if it doesn't help, transformer is less likely to. With 5 experiments remaining, this high-information experiment will guide whether to invest further in multiprofile or pivot toward multimodal fusion with a stronger image encoder (e.g., ViT-L).

The current best is config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) at 0.650 accuracy, showing that multiprofile aggregation provides a large boost over singleprofile (0.520→0.650). The key open question is whether transformer aggregation outperforms simple avgpool for this same encoder+profile combination. config_006 changes only the aggregation method (avgpool→transformer) while holding rna_encoder=scvi_n200 and profile_setting=multiprofile constant, giving a clean single-variable comparison. This is the highest-value next experiment because: (1) it directly exploits the strongest evidence found so far, (2) it isolates the aggregation effect to inform whether the remaining 4 experiments should invest in transformer-based multimodal configurations or stick with avgpool, and (3) it reduces uncertainty about a critical design choice before committing budget to more complex multimodal fusion experiments.

Evidence: RNA-only multi-profile with scvi_n200 is the clear best so far (0.653 with transformer, 0.650 with avgpool), and image-only ResNet50 is very weak (0.208). The dominant open question is whether adding an image modality to the best RNA configuration can push accuracy above 0.653. This experiment (config_039) extends the best RNA setup (scvi_n200, multi-profile, transformer) by adding the strongest available image encoder (ViT-L, untested) with weighted fusion, which allows the model to adaptively down-weight the image signal if it is uninformative. This isolates the effect of modality addition while holding all RNA-side choices at their empirically best values. It is the best use of experiment 7 because it directly tests the single most impactful remaining design question (does multimodal help?) before the budget runs out, and the result will determine whether the final 2 experiments should refine a multimodal config or confirm RNA-only as optimal.

The current best is config_039 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.725 accuracy. The only multimodal experiment so far uses weighted fusion, so we have no evidence on whether concat fusion could match or exceed it. Config_038 is a clean single-variable comparison (weighted→concat) that isolates the fusion strategy while holding all other components constant. This is critical because with only 2 experiments remaining after this one, I need to confirm whether the 0.725 result is robust to a simpler fusion mechanism or whether weighted fusion is a key contributor. If concat performs comparably, the current best is confirmed and I can use remaining budget for a different axis; if weighted is clearly superior, it validates the current configuration as the likely final answer.

The current best is config_039 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250 acc. The only untested variant within this top-performing family is the aggregation method: avgpool vs. transformer. In the RNA-only multiprofile setting, transformer narrowly beat avgpool (0.6530 vs 0.6501), but that gap was small and the multimodal context (with a strong ViT image encoder) could shift the balance. Config_037 (avgpool + weighted, same encoders and fusion) isolates the aggregation effect as a single-variable comparison against config_039. If avgpool matches or exceeds transformer here, it reveals a simpler, potentially more robust configuration; if not, it confirms transformer aggregation is the critical component and config_039 is near-optimal. With only 1 experiment remaining after this, confirming the aggregation choice within the best family is the highest-value use of the slot—any other direction (e.g., resnet50, scgpt, PCA) is strongly disfavored by existing evidence.

The current best (config_039: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile + transformer + weighted, acc=0.725) combines all individually best components. The main remaining uncertainty is whether the 200-dim scvi bottleneck vs. 2000-dim PCA representation interacts differently with the strong ViT image encoder in the multimodal setting. In rna_only, scvi_n200 (0.520) beat pca_n2000 (0.485) by ~0.035, but with a powerful image modality providing complementary spatial information, the higher-dimensional PCA may retain gene-level detail that the 200-dim scvi bottleneck discards. Config_027 changes only the RNA encoder (scvi_n200→pca_n2000) while holding all other settings at their empirically best values, making it a clean single-variable comparison against config_039. It is the highest-expected-value untested configuration and the most informative final experiment: if it approaches or exceeds 0.725, it reveals a meaningful encoder×modality interaction; if it falls short, it confirms scvi_n200 as the optimal RNA representation in the multimodal regime.
